hypotheses.justification: Only local bounds are needed. At each t₀, continuity and IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn bound ‖F‖ on [t₀ - 1 - T, t₀ + 1]; enlarge this bound to M ≥ 0. For |t - t₀| < 1 and τ ∈ (0,T], this bounds ‖F (t - τ)‖. Repeat the existing dominated-convergence proof with M replacing C: intervalIntegral.continuousAt_of_dominated_interval requires domination only near t₀. The same integrable Abel kernel applies. At τ = 0 the integrand is zero, and T = 0 gives a zero integral.
Recover it as (norm_nonneg (F 0)).trans (hFC 0), then use the existing proof. This also covers C = 0. Both hC and hFC can in fact be removed together using the local-bound argument.

Split on 0 ≤ T and use the existing proof in that case. Otherwise T < 0, and every τ in the unordered interval between 0 and T satisfies τ ≤ 0. By definition mildShiftedStokesIntegrand is then zero for every evaluation time. intervalIntegral.integral_congr and intervalIntegral.integral_zero show the trajectory is constantly zero. The endpoint T = 0 also gives a zero integral.
